transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, the clinical conversational agent. I conducted your post-cataract surgery follow-up check, and I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. To start, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as watering plants or gentle weeding, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting, bending, or strenuous gardening for a month. If you're unsure, it's always best to err on the side of caution and wait a bit longer. Have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery. Wearing sunglasses when you're outside can help. If your sensitivity is severe or you're experiencing pain, it's best to let your care team know so we can assess it further. Have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad I could help clarify that for you. Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery. But this should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. Have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: All your questions have been answered. .
